title: Machine-readable failures for every client command and a consistent selected project
summary: Every client command failure, including an argument-parse error, must end in a non-zero exit and, in machine-readable mode, exactly one structured report with a false success flag, the command the user asked for and the project in effect; human-readable mode prints the message on the error channel only. The selected project must be passed to the engine by every command that acts on a project and must not be passed by a command that does not, and the reported project must equal the project actually sent.
requirements: Every client command that acts on a project sends the selected project to the engine, and the project reported to the caller is exactly the project that was sent.
Every client command that does not act on a project sends no project to the engine and reports none.

Every failed invocation exits with a non-zero status. Failures include at least: an unknown command, a missing required argument, a numeric limit given a non-numeric value, remarks for a returned task that contain no text, and a refusal reported by the engine.
In machine-readable mode every failed invocation produces exactly one structured failure report in the machine-readable output and nothing else in that output.
That failure report carries a success indication set to false and a readable message stating what went wrong.

That failure report names the command the user asked for and the project in effect at the time of the invocation whenever the invocation determines them; a value stays empty only when the invocation itself cannot determine it.
In human-readable mode a failed invocation prints the readable message on the error output and produces no structured report.
No failed invocation ends through an unhandled argument error, and no failed invocation shows an internal error trace in either output mode.
A refusal reported by the engine remains a failure even when the engine itself reports success, and the failure report keeps the engine's own error details unchanged.
The successful answer of every command keeps its current shape and content, and successful invocations continue to exit with success.

Asking for machine-readable output with a missing required argument produces one structured failure report with a false success indication, the requested command, the project in effect and a readable message, and a non-zero exit status.
Asking for machine-readable output with an unknown command produces the same structured failure report, naming the command exactly as the user typed it.
A non-numeric limit passed to a command produces the same structured failure report instead of an internal error trace.
Returning a task with remarks that carry no text is refused with the same structured failure report and no request reaches the engine.
In human-readable mode each of these same failures prints the message on the error output, produces no structured report, and exits with a non-zero status.
acceptance: With machine-readable output requested and a required argument missing, the invocation exits non-zero and produces exactly one structured failure report carrying a false success indication, the requested command, the project in effect and a readable message.
With machine-readable output requested and an unknown command, the invocation exits non-zero and produces the same structured failure report, naming the command exactly as the user typed it.
A numeric limit given a non-numeric value produces the same structured failure report instead of an internal error trace.
Returning a task whose remarks contain no text produces the same structured failure report and no request reaches the engine.
In human-readable mode each of the above failures prints the message on the error output, produces no structured report, and exits non-zero.
Every command that acts on a project sends the selected project to the engine and reports exactly that project; every command that does not act on a project sends none.
A refusal reported by the engine whose own success indication is true is still reported as a failure, with the engine's own error details preserved.
Successful answers of every command keep their current shape and content and exit with success.
The failure message is readable and states what went wrong.
constraints: The client stays a thin wrapper: it never invents engine behaviour and never reads project files itself.
Only the failure report changes; successful answers keep their current shape.
All committed artifacts are in English.
assumptions: The next requirement is the first item of the recorded priority list: the project in all commands together with machine-readable argument errors.
The project in effect for a failed invocation is the project stored in the client session, which is written only after the engine accepted it.
The failure report keeps the field names the client already uses for a failed command, adding only the values that were previously empty.
A command that lists projects is treated as not acting on a project.
